subject: Aligning midterm capacity uplift and single-co-term path — BrightScale discussion
messages:
From: Emma Chen <emma@brightscale.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Moya <carlos@brightscale.com>, procurement@brightscale.com
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity uplift + co-term alignment

Hi Vivek,

We've seen an unexpected spike in model usage over the last three weeks as two of our products hit GA. We need to increase committed capacity for the rest of the year — roughly +60% of our current monthly commit — and we'd like to align the new capacity to a single renewal date (co-term) so bookkeeping is simpler.

Can you send over the options (prorated top-up vs annualized uplift), and what discounts or credits might be available for mid-contract expansion? Procurement will likely ask for a path that minimizes short-term spend but preserves predictability.

Thanks,
Emma Chen
Head of Platform
BrightScale
emma@brightscale.com

[Attachment: spike_usage_summary.csv]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emma Chen <emma@brightscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift + co-term alignment

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and congrats on GA.

Quick read: two practical paths we typically offer:
- Option 1: One-time prorated top-up (effective immediately). No change to your renewal date; we prorate the added capacity to your next invoice. We can offer an 8% top-up discount on the incremental capacity.
- Option 2: Annualize the uplift and co-term to a single date (you pick a co-term window). This gives predictable unit pricing and we can provide a deeper discount (we can go to ~12–13% depending on committed months). In that case we apply the new pricing to the remainder of the co-term and give a small voucher for the remaining partial month.

I'll pull together numbers and a short spreadsheet. Looping Marissa and Ben for guidance on discounting and whether we should offer a one-month credit as part of the co-term path.

Vivek
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-22T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift + co-term alignment

Internal — rough math and risks.

Vivek, Marissa — I plugged their GA numbers into our unit-cost model. Key points:
- Incremental cost to us for +60% (mixed GPU types) is low if committed; marginal infra cost ~20% of list.
- If we ask for annualized commitment through 2028-01-31 (co-term), we can safely offer 13% discount on new capacity and include a 1-month credit voucher to compensate for the partial period.
- If they prefer a short-term prorated top-up, 8% is safe without exec signoff.
- Going to 15%+ requires VP approval and potentially an uplift on SLA/priority support (we should test appetite).

I recommend we present both options clearly and highlight the net cost per token over the 12-month horizon to influence procurement toward the annualized co-term.

[Internal attachment: uplift_margin_calc_v1.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift + co-term alignment

Agree with Ben's approach. Final constraints from me:
- External offer: 8% for prorated top-up (no co-term).
- For an annualized/co-term path: offer 13% on the uplift if they commit through 2028-01-31 and accept standard billing (no retroactive refunds). Add a one-month credit (voucher) applied against the first renewed invoice after co-term.
- We can go to 15% but only with VP signoff and if they accept a 9–12 month minimum ramp schedule.

I'll sign off on the two-option document. Please attach the pricing workbook (uplift_pricing_v3.xlsx) and the 1-page co-term summary (co-term_consolidation_summary.pdf) when we send to the customer.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Aligning midterm capacity uplift and single-co-term path — BrightScale discussion

Hi Emma (and team),

Thanks for the patience — attached are two clean options based on your spike and our internal math. I've included a one-page summary and a workbook with the line-item math.

Option A — Prorated Top-up (fastest)
- Immediate +60% on current commit
- Applied on next invoice prorated for remaining billing period
- Discount: 8% on incremental units
- No change to your current renewal date

Option B — Annualize & Co-term to 2028-01-31 (recommended for predictability)
- Increase commit to cover +60% (annualized pricing)
- New co-term date: 2028-01-31
- Discount on uplift: 13%
- One-month credit voucher applied on first invoice after co-term

Why Option B? It reduces net unit cost over 12 months and simplifies procurement (single renewal). If you want deeper economics (15%+), I can escalate but will need VP approval and a brief commitment window discussion.

Next steps:
1) Tell me which option you prefer — I can turn the chosen option into a short amendment and send to procurement.
2) If you want, let's schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk the numbers with Ben and Marissa. Calendly: https://calendly.com/vivek-redwood/30

Attachments: co-term_consolidation_summary.pdf, uplift_pricing_v3.xlsx
